menu.quit_submessage: The system collapses in your absence.

game.title: SACRIFICE
game.win_message: You have successfully navigated the complexities of your kingdom for {{years}} years.
game.loss_message: Your rule has come to a tragic end in year {{year}}, Term {{term}}.
game.exit_confirm_desc: Are you sure you want to return to the hub? Current progress will be lost.
game.hover_instruction: Hover over an option to view advisor projections...

report.open_borders: Open borders have slightly eroded traditional Piety.
report.martial_law: Martial law is choking the local Bazaar.
report.secularism: Secularism forces the Sepah to exert more control.
report.legitimacy_spent: Political Legitimacy was spent to stabilize the nation.

end_game.default_loss: The system has reached a terminal state.

slides: The revolution is over. The old regime has fallen. You stand victorious in the ashes.
But victory is fragile. The Sepah demands control. The Bonyads demand wealth. The Ideology demands obedience. You cannot satisfy them all.
You are the Supreme Leader. How long can you survive the system you created?

death_reasons.sepah_min: Without the military to protect the borders, foreign adversaries and internal separatists have fractured the nation.
death_reasons.sepah_max: The generals have decided they no longer need a civilian government. A military coup has deposed you.
death_reasons.piety_min: The clerics have declared you an apostate. The streets fill with zealots calling for your head.
death_reasons.piety_max: The hardliners have completely taken over. You are no longer the leader, merely a figurehead for ideological purity.
death_reasons.bazaar_min: The economy has completely collapsed. Bread riots have turned into a full-scale revolution.
death_reasons.bazaar_max: The Bonyads and oligarchs have bought the entire state. You have been quietly replaced by a corporate puppet.
death_reasons.isolation_min: The borders opened completely. Unrestricted foreign influence has overwhelmed the state, forcing a regime change.
death_reasons.isolation_max: The country is entirely cut off from the world. Total systemic collapse has occurred due to a lack of basic imports.

p1.description: The Clerical Council proposes a strict religious mandate. This holy decree will bolster tradition, but it requires military enforcement and adds new taxes that will drain merchant profits.

advisorQuotes.sepah: My soldiers are ready to enforce your will, but deployment costs are rising.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The merchants are already struggling with tariffs. This decree will break them.
advisorQuotes.isolation: National tradition is our shield. We must remain pure, even if it hurts the markets.

p2.description: A purge of ‘internal agitators’ is proposed. This will improve internal security and satisfy the devout, but the international community will judge us harshly, damaging our global legitimacy.

advisorQuotes.sepah: We've identified the threats. Give the order, and we ensure total stability.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Foreign investors are already nervous. A purge will send them running.
advisorQuotes.isolation: The world's opinion is irrelevant. We must ensure our house is in order.

p3.description: The Ministry proposes a grand temple expansion project. It will please the faithful but requires a significant levy on the merchant class.

advisorQuotes.sepah: It's a lot of stone and labor that could be used for fortifications.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The guild is furious. You're bleeding the markets dry for mere monuments.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Let us build monuments to our own strength, not to global trade.

p4.description: A decree to censor secular literature in national schools. This will safeguard tradition but lower our standing among the youth and educators.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Ignorance is easier to manage than rebellion. I support the ban.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Education is the foundation of a modern economy. This is a step backward.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Protect our children's minds from foreign contamination at all costs.

p5.description: A proposal to ban all foreign pilgrims. It ensures absolute religious purity but creates a diplomatic vacuum and hurts our external relations.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Tracking outsiders is a nightmare. Closing the gates simplifies security.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The pilgrims bring foreign coin and trade. Cutting them off is economic suicide.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Our soil is for our people. Let the foreigners pray in their own lands.

p6.description: The Clerics request the authority to oversee all public tribunals. This will centralize faith but potentially alienate the secular bureaucracy.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Military tribunals are more efficient, but I can work with the clerics.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: This will lead to arbitrary rulings that threaten merchant contracts.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Internal justice must be absolute and free from external influence.

p7.description: A mandate to convert merchant warehouses into community kitchens. It feeds the poor but creates a massive rift with the Bazaar guild.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A full stomach keeps the riots away. Strategically sound.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: This is theft! You are seizing private property and killing commerce.
advisorQuotes.isolation: We must provide for our own. Self-reliance begins with a full granary.

p8.description: The High Temple asks for a dedicated security detail from the army. This intermingling of church and state creates a powerful, unified front.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Distracting my best men for ceremonial guard duty? Acceptable, for now.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: When the army and clergy unite, the merchant has no voice left.
advisorQuotes.isolation: A unified internal front is the only way to resist the encroaching world.

p9.description: A holy day is declared as a mandatory national strike. Devotion will skyrocket, but the economy will stall and legitimacy takes a hit from the chaos.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Empty streets are easy to patrol, but the idle mind is dangerous.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: A day without trade? Across the whole nation? It's madness!
advisorQuotes.isolation: Silence the noise of the world so the nation can refocus on its core.

p10.description: New sumptuary laws are proposed to restrict luxury spending. This enforces modesty but enrages the merchants who sell high-end goods.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Men should be hard, not soft from luxury. I approve.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Luxury goods are our highest margin exports! This will kill the Bazaar.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Foreign decadence has no place here. We value rugged self-sufficiency.

p11.description: A request to replace the local police with religious morality guards. Security will be absolute, though public trust may plummet.

advisorQuotes.sepah: The Morality Police are fanatical, but effective at maintaining order.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Bullying merchants over their 'devotion' will stop every sale.
advisorQuotes.isolation: We must police the soul of the nation as strictly as we police the borders.

p12.description: The state is asked to officially recognize a controversial religious sect. It expands our reach but triggers massive international pushback.

advisorQuotes.sepah: If they provide soldiers, I don't care what they believe.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Sanctions will follow this. The world doesn't like radicals.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Who cares what the world thinks? If they are loyal to the flag, they are ours.

p13.description: A proposal to spend the national surplus on monumental holy statues. It’s a bold display of faith that leaves the Bazaar struggling for liquid capital.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Statues don't win wars, but they do make for imposing landmarks.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: That gold should be in circulation, not cast in bronze for 'spirituality'.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Let the world look at our borders and see only our strength and conviction.

p14.description: The Clerics lobby for control over the national archives. This secures our history but makes the secular bureaucrats extremely restless.

advisorQuotes.sepah: As long as military secrets stay with me, they can have the dusty old books.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Information is a commodity. Letting the Clerics guard it is a bottleneck.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Control the history, control the future. Guard our secrets fiercely.

p15.description: A call for 'The Great Tithe' to fund a new religious garrison. The Sepah will grow stronger, though at the expense of merchant freedom.

advisorQuotes.sepah: New recruits and fresh gear. I won't turn down extra funding.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Another levy? You're treating the Bazaar like a bottomless well.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Every coin spent internally is a coin not sent to a foreign bank.

p16.description: A ban on foreign technology in temple grounds. It preserves tradition but cuts us off from essential modern maintenance services.

advisorQuotes.sepah: I prefer reliable local tech anyway. Foreign circuits can be bugged.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Modern maintenance is a global service. This ban will lead to blackouts.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Our dependency on foreign machines is a weakness. Rip them out.

p17.description: The Clerical Council asks to seize unused merchant land for new shrines. It’s a divine land-grab that the Bazaar will never forget.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Land is land. Better a shrine than a potential rebel hideout.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Unused? That land is reserved for future expansion! This is theft.
advisorQuotes.isolation: National land for national purposes. The merchants should stop complaining.

p18.description: A request to make ancient hymns the only permitted public music. Faith will become the national pulse, though the merchants fear lost sales.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Better hymns than the rhythmic shouting of the protesters.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Entertainment is a massive sector. You're killing the cafes and theaters.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Our songs are our own. The noise of global pop culture must be silenced.

s1.description: The High Command requests massive funding for an impenetrable border wall. This will ensure order and security, but will drain the Bazaar and heighten our global isolation.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A wall is not just stone; it's the ultimate statement of our sovereignty.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Isolating us will only lead to stagnation and high import costs.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Build it twice as thick. No one comes in, no one goes out.

s2.description: A decree for mass conscription to strengthen our defenses. Thousands of young men will be moved from factories to frontlines, bolstering the Sepah but potentially paralyzing the economy.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Soldiers are the true foundation of a nation, not factory workers.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: We're losing our workforce! Productivity will plummet overnight.
advisorQuotes.isolation: A nation in arms is a nation that cannot be bullied by foreigners.

s3.description: The military proposes a total curfew in the capital due to 'security concerns'. It crushes dissent but shuts down all Bazaar activity.

advisorQuotes.sepah: The streets must be clear for our tanks. Order is paramount.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The night market is our lifeblood! This will bankrupt the vendors.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Lock the doors. Domestic peace is worth a thousand lost sales.

s4.description: A plan to seize all chemical factories for the production of armor. It strengthens our defense but cuts us off from international trade norms.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Steel and composite plating will save our boys. The cost doesn't matter.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Those chemicals are for fertilizers and exports! You're killing our trade.
advisorQuotes.isolation: We must be self-reliant. If the world shuns us for our defense, so be it.

s5.description: The Sepah requests the power to audit all religious sermons for 'subversive' content. This unifies internal power but risks a rift with the Clerics.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Even a priest can be a spy. No one is above the state's security.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Religious unrest is bad for business. Stay out of the temples.
advisorQuotes.isolation: One voice, one nation. Dissent, even from the pulpit, is a threat.

s6.description: A proposal to build a massive naval port for armored vessels. Merchant traffic will be displaced, though our coastal reach will be absolute.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Our borders don't end at the shore. We need a fleet of iron.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The existing port handles all our global trade. Don't block the docks!
advisorQuotes.isolation: The sea is just another border to be closed to the unwanted.

s7.description: The military asks to repossess artisan silver for use in heavy plating. Defense will be upgraded, but the Bazaar faces a craft-stock crisis.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Precious metals are better suited for armor than for trinkets.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Jewelry and silver-work are our most famous exports! This is madness.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Luxury is a distraction. Silver serves the state better as a shield.

s8.description: A mandate to militarize the national rail lines. Logistics for the army will be flawless, though the world will see us as preparing for war.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Mobility is the key to victory. The state needs total rail control.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: How are we supposed to move grain and textiles? This is a bottleneck.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Control the tracks, control the flow of the nation. Keep foreigners off.

s9.description: A request for a 'Security Levy' paid directly to the officer corps. The Sepah will be loyal, but the public sees this as pure corruption.

advisorQuotes.sepah: My officers need to be well-paid to resist the temptation of bribes.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Call it what it is: a protection racket. The merchants won't be happy.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Internal stability has a price. Pay it, or the world will walk in.

s10.description: The High Command proposes a 'Shield the Nation' drill that lasts a month. Total security readiness, but we are effectively severed from the world.

advisorQuotes.sepah: The people must be ready for the inevitable. It's a drill for survival.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: A month with no imports? We'll be eating bark by week three!
advisorQuotes.isolation: Excellent. Close the gates, cut the cables. Let us see who we really are.

s11.description: A decree to replace all civilian judges with military officers. This ensures swift justice but destroys any remaining public trust.

advisorQuotes.sepah: The law is simple: OBEY. We don't need lawyers, we need discipline.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Contract law is too complex for soldiers. This will create chaos.
advisorQuotes.isolation: External values have no place in our courts. Military law is pure.

s12.description: The Sepah requests the decommissioning of the national trade fleet for military conversions. Our navy will be peerless, but trade will suffer.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A merchant ship is just a target. A warship is a deterrent.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: You're cutting our legs off! How can we trade without a fleet?
advisorQuotes.isolation: Our ships should carry cannons, not foreign consumer goods.

s13.description: A plan to establish permanent checkpoints on all merchant roads. Smuggling stops, but the flow of goods is severely throttled.

advisorQuotes.sepah: If it's on the road, it's under our eyes. No more illegal traffic.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Checkpoints add hours to every journey. It's killing the logistics.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Total knowledge of internal movements is the key to total sovereignty.

s14.description: The military asks for the right to 'Emergency Requisition' from any temple. It’s an efficient move that borders on blasphemy.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Space and resources are needed for the defense of all. No exceptions.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Taking from temples is a risky move, but efficiently managed.
advisorQuotes.isolation: The state is the ultimate sacred entity. No institution is exempt.

s15.description: A proposal to give soldiers full immunity for their duties. Loyalty will be absolute, but legitimacy among the common folk is sacrificed.

advisorQuotes.sepah: If a soldier fears a lawsuit, he won't pull the trigger. Give them immunity.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: A soldier above the law is a bandit in uniform. Bad for stability.
advisorQuotes.isolation: The defenders of the nation must be unshackled from civilian whims.

s16.description: The Sepah requests the construction of a massive underground 'Command Bunker'. It ensures survival but draws suspicious eyes from abroad.

advisorQuotes.sepah: We must be prepared for the worst. Survival of the state is priority.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The cost is astronomical. We should be investing in port infrastructure.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Let the world spy; they will find only a fortress hidden in the bedrock.

s17.description: A mandate to nationalize all fuel reserves for military use only. Our tanks will never stall, but the foreign supply lines will tighten.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Without fuel, the army is just a collection of heavy statues.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Industry needs fuel too! You're grinding the factories to a halt.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Not a drop of our energy should be traded away to foreign competitors.

s18.description: The military asks to oversee the printing of the national news. Information control is absolute, though it cost us every shred of public trust.

advisorQuotes.sepah: The press is a weapon. We must control the narrative of the nation.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Market confidence relies on transparency. Censor the news, and we fail.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Foreign propaganda must be countered with a single, national truth.

b1.description: Foreign corporations offer to privatize and modernize our national ports. This massive infusion of capital will revitalize the Bazaar, but the military warns of a total loss of sovereignty.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Giving our ports to foreigners? You're letting the enemy in the back door.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Capital is the lifeblood of our future. We must modernize or die.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Selling our ports is selling our soul. Reject the foreign vultures.

b2.description: A proposal to allow the unrestricted import of foreign luxury goods. It will keep the wealth circulating and the people happy, but the Clerics condemn it as a celebration of secular vanity and greed.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Luxury breeds weakness. I'd rather see that money go to the armories.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The people want options! Happiness and trade go hand in hand.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Imported decadence poisons the national character. Keep it out.

b3.description: A request to deregulate the mining guild. Output will skyrocket, but the Sepah fears illegal smuggling and the loss of state control.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Smuggling from mines is how rebels get their gold. Keep the regulations.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Let the markets breathe! We're sitting on a mountain of untapped wealth.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Our minerals are for our factories, not for foreign export markets.

b4.description: A plan to open a free-trade zone in the capital. Global capital will flow, but it requires dissolving many traditional religious tariffs.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A free-trade zone is a spy-zone. I want my men at every corner.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: This will put us on the global map! The capital will be a beacon of wealth.
advisorQuotes.isolation: A zone without borders is a zone without sovereignty. Reject it.

b5.description: The Bazaar guild asks for an 'Economic Stimulus' funded by the military budget. It pays off merchant debts but leaves the Sepah with empty storehouses.

advisorQuotes.sepah: You want to take from the defense of the nation to pay for merchant mistakes?
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The merchants are the engine of this country. If we stall, everything else falls.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Funding internal trade is good, but raiding the armory is risky.

b6.description: A proposal to host an international trade expo. It’s a merchant’s dream, but it brings in foreign observers who the Sepah doesn't trust.

advisorQuotes.sepah: An 'Expo' is just a cover for foreign intelligence agents. Reject it.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The world's eyes will be on us! The prestige alone will be worth millions.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Inviting the world in is inviting their spying and their corruption.

b7.description: The merchants request the abolishment of 'Holy Day' closures. Profits will increase, but the Clerics will view this as an open declaration of war.

advisorQuotes.sepah: I don't care about the days, as long as the factories produce gear.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Keeping shops closed for half the week is economic insanity! Open them.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Internal customs are what define us. Efficiency is secondary.

b8.description: A mandate to standardize all national weights and measures. It complicates religious traditions but makes our trade exponentially more efficient.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Everything should be standardized. In the army and in the shop. I agree.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Efficient trade is honest trade. No more confusion at the docks!
advisorQuotes.isolation: Metric or imperial, it must be OUR system, not a global one.

b9.description: A request to lower taxes on all imported silk and spice. It bolsters the Bazaar but leaves the Sepah without the funding they were promised.

advisorQuotes.sepah: We need that tax revenue for the border wall. Don't cut the military.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Silk and spice are luxury essentials. Lowering taxes will spur growth.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Tax foreign goods until they are too expensive to be worth the trouble.

b10.description: A plan to incentivize local craftsmanship over foreign goods. The Bazaar grows, but our international partners will see this as a hostile act.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Buy local, build local. It's better for security and independence.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: It protects our artisans, but it will trigger trade wars with our neighbors.
advisorQuotes.isolation: A true nation buys only from itself. Reject the foreign junk.

b11.description: A proposal to build an international merchant railway. It connects us to the world but requires a massive surrender of military land.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A railway as a vulnerability. An enemy could use it to reach our heart.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: This is the superhighway of the future! We must build the tracks.
advisorQuotes.isolation: A railway is a bridge. Bridges let the world's problems walk right in.

b12.description: The merchants ask for a 'Market Stability Law' that allows them to self-regulate. Legitimacy rises with their support, but you lose control over them.

advisorQuotes.sepah: If you lose control of the gold, you lose control of the nation.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Trust us. We know how to manage the markets better than any bureaucrat.
advisorQuotes.isolation: National markets should serve national interests, not merchant whims.

b13.description: A plan to export our national grain for foreign silver. The Bazaar will be rich, but the Clerics fear for the local poor who will go hungry.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A hungry citizen is a riotous citizen. Be careful with the food supply.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Silver will buy us the tech we need. It's a strategic export.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Food is a weapon. Keep it here. We don't need their silver.

b14.description: A request for a national gold standard. It makes us a global player but removes the flexibility we need for religious funding.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Gold is solid. Paper is weak. I support the move to the standard.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: It gives our currency international respect. Essential for growth.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Tie the currency to the earth itself. Self-reliance in every coin.

b15.description: A proposal to give the Bazaar guild a seat on the National Council. Their loyalty will be bought, but at a huge cost to your authority.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Adding a merchant to the council will only complicate our security plans.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: We deserve a voice in the leadership of the nation we fund.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Private interests have no place in a unified national council.

b16.description: A ban on all street protests to 'protect merchant storefronts'. It creates economic peace but the people will not forget the crackdown.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Finally! No more riots, no more chaos. Let me clear the asphalt.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Protests disrupt trade and damage property. We need physical stability.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Public order is the prerequisite for a strong and unified state.

b17.description: A request to subsidize national shipbuilders. It creates jobs and wealth, though the Sepah feels their base funding is being diverted.

advisorQuotes.sepah: If they aren't warships, I don't see why the army budget should pay.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Maritime power is the key to global commerce. We must build better ships.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Control the waves with our own hulls. No more foreign shipping.

b18.description: A plan to establish a central bank overseen by the Bazaar. Legitimacy is spent for their absolute cooperation in the coming years.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A bank with its own rules is a threat to the state's sovereignty.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Give us the keys to the treasury, and we will make the nation rich.
advisorQuotes.isolation: One central vault for one central nation. Keep the world's money out.

i1.description: Global leaders invite us to open our borders to unrestricted trade. Our exporters will flourish, but the Sepah warns of foreign subversion and the Clerics fear cultural erosion.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Unrestricted trade is just another word for unrestricted spying.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The world is waiting for our goods! Open the gates and let the coin flow.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Opening the gates is the beginning of the end for our sovereignty.

i2.description: A multi-national aid package is offered in exchange for signing a major foreign trade pact. This will stabilize our currency and strengthen the Bazaar, but it restricts our military budget.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Aid with strings attached is just a bribe from our enemies. Reject it.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: We need that capital to rebuild our markets. It's a survival necessity.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Begging for foreign crumbs makes our nation look weak and desperate.

i3.description: A proposal to host a UN-style human rights summit. It shows our growth to the world but requires a massive sacrifice of internal military control.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Letting foreign 'observers' in? You might as well give them the keys.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The global prestige would be enormous. Think of the future investment.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Foreign 'observers' are just spies in suits. Keep the doors locked.

i4.description: A plan to link our national communication grid to the global network. The Bazaar will boom, though the Sepah warns of a loss of information control.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Connecting to their grid lets their viruses directly into our systems.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Information speed is the new currency. We cannot be left in the dark.
advisorQuotes.isolation: The global network is a pipeline for cultural rot. Stay disconnected.

i5.description: A total withdrawal from all international treaties is proposed. We will be absolutely pure and self-reliant, though the rest of the world will turn its back.

advisorQuotes.sepah: No more treaties, no more compromises. We stand alone and strong.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: This is isolationist suicide. The Bazaar will starve in total solitude.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Tear up the papers. We answer to no one but ourselves.

i6.description: A request to sign a 'Global Peace Accord'. It lowers our military readiness but creates a golden age for merchant trade across the borders.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Peace is just the period between wars. Don't let your guard down.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Trade flourishes in peace. Sign the accord and let the markets bloom.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Peace is a trap used by the inclusive to disarm the vigilant.

i7.description: A decree to deport all foreign diplomats for 'national security'. We are a island of order now, though we stand almost completely alone.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Diplomats are just spies in fancy suits. Get them out of our hair.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Who will negotiate our trade deals? You're burning every bridge.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Sweep them out. They are guests who have overstayed their welcome.

i8.description: A plan to allow foreign missionaries to build schools. It opens our borders and minds, though it risks the fundamental stability of our faith.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Missionaries today, subversives tomorrow. Do not let them educate.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Modern education attracts foreign talent and investment. I approve.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Indoctrination by foreigners is the first step to cultural submission.

i9.description: A proposal to join a regional military alliance. We surrender our total independence for a massive boost in external trade and security.

advisorQuotes.sepah: An alliance means fighting their wars too. We should defend ourselves.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The regional market access will be worth the loss of autonomy.
advisorQuotes.isolation: We do not need 'allies' who only wish to use our soldiers for their ends.

i10.description: A demand for all foreign assets to be seized by the state. We are independent and well-funded, but we are effectively a pariah state now.

advisorQuotes.sepah: If it's on our soil, it's ours. Seize it and fund the army.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: They will retaliate by seizing OUR assets abroad. This will be ruinous.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Everything within our borders belongs to the state. No exceptions.

i11.description: A request to sign a 'Common Market' agreement. It ties our fate to our neighbors, bolstering trade but surrendering national control.

advisorQuotes.sepah: A common market means common borders. I cannot ensure security.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: This is the path to prosperity! A unified market is a stable market.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Common markets lead to common problems. We prefer our own issues.

i12.description: A proposal to host the World Games. It's a massive expense and attracts foreign scrutiny, but the Bazaar will witness a once-in-a-century boom.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Millions of visitors? It's a security nightmare on a global scale.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: The tourism revenue alone will fund the national debt. Host the games!
advisorQuotes.isolation: The world's circus has no place in our silent and serious nation.

i13.description: A plan to allow foreign banks to set up national branches. Our economy will stabilize, though the Clerics fear we are selling our souls for coin.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Foreign banks are just channels for foreign money to influence our politics.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: We need their capital and expertise. Our local banks are antiquated.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Finance is the chain the world uses to bind independent nations.

i14.description: A request to allow foreign tourists unrestricted travel. Profits will flow like water, though the Clerics fear for our traditional public modesty.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Tourists wander into secure areas. I want them restricted to hotels.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: Tourism is pure profit with no overhead! Open every scenic route.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Tourists are just amateur spies Gawking at our heritage. Keep them out.

i15.description: A total 'Open Sky' agreement for foreign airlines. We are a hub of the world, though the Sepah will no longer control our airspace.

advisorQuotes.sepah: The sky is our first line of defense. Losing control is catastrophic.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: A global hub brings global gold. Open the skies and let them land.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Our air should only carry our planes. The sky is a national boundary.

i16.description: A plan to allow foreign-owned mines in our territory. We get a share of the wealth without the risk, though we stand further from the world's norms.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Foreigners digging in our earth? They will find more than just ore.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: They bring the tech and the labor. We just collect the checks. Smart.
advisorQuotes.isolation: Every ounce of our soil is our birthright. We do not sell the deep earth.

i17.description: A proposal to import foreign medical experts and teachers. Our people will stay healthy, though the Clerics warn of indoctrination by the profane.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Foreign teachers will only preach their 'human rights' nonsense to the kids.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: A healthy workforce is a productive workforce. Bring in the doctors.
advisorQuotes.isolation: We prefer our own sickness to the cure of a foreign master.

i18.description: A mandate to dissolve our borders and join a 'Global Federation'. A total loss of independent sovereignty for the sake of survival.

advisorQuotes.sepah: Dissolving the borders? That is the day the army ceases to exist. I refuse.
advisorQuotes.bazaar: A world without borders is a world with perfect trade. It is the future.
advisorQuotes.isolation: I would rather see the world burn than see our borders erased.
